svg.title: Why scaling up after FSMap rollback created an empty directory hierarchy
svg.desc: MON loads an older FSMap with max_mds=1 and an orphaned rank 0. Raising the target to 2 makes is_in treat rank 0 as new. promote selects CREATING, and boot_create initializes a fresh journal and an empty root hierarchy.
svg.text: The MONs recovered. Why were the old directories still gone?
FSMap versions and rank state are on the left. MDS metadata is on the right. Reverting the former does not roll back the latter.
Steps within stages; matching numbers link calls and bodies

g.text: MON storage and the live FSMap
MON branches selected by the state
Historical maps and loading pointer, shown schematically
Older map avoids shrinking with rank 0 still orphaned
Existing-rank takeover would replay the journal
Once rank 0 is active, assign rank 1
Separate from MON FSMap version storage
Old directory entries are no longer visible
is_in() reads up / failed, not the raw in set
MON publishes MDSMap, MDS follows its assigned state
Key distinction active means the daemon is serving. CREATING initializes a new journal and root instead of replaying the old rank's log.
Source src/mon/MDSMonitor.cc · src/mds/{MDSMap.h,FSMap.cc,MDSRank.cc,MDCache.cc} | e_old / e_bad are symbolic epochs
